controls.title: Assess whether security controls work
controls.statement: Plan and perform evidence-based assessments that determine whether security controls are correctly implemented, operating as intended and effective for their risk.
controls.risk: Leaders may rely on controls that exist on paper but fail in practice, allowing preventable incidents and overstating the organisation's security position.
controls.scope: Security controls in systems and operating environments, assessment plans, assessors, procedures, evidence, reports and assurance schedules.
controls.examine: Compare the assessment schedule and approved plans with system risk, control scope, assessor competence and independence, procedures used, evidence retained and final reports.
controls.interview: Ask authorising officers, control owners and assessors how scope and depth are chosen, conflicts are managed and effectiveness conclusions are supported.
controls.test: Select completed assessments and independently repeat a small sample of procedures, checking whether the evidence supports the reported design, implementation and operating conclusions.
controls.expected: Assessments cover the relevant controls and environment, use suitable assessors and repeatable procedures, and reach conclusions supported by current evidence.

mappings.basis: Requires security control assessments to determine whether controls are implemented correctly and operating as intended.
Defines the scope, strengths, weaknesses, risks, effectiveness and remediation content of a security assessment report.
Requires an approved control-assessment plan, suitable assessors and recurring assessment of control effectiveness.
Requires independent assessors or assessment teams for control assessments.
Requires security risk management activity to be subject to ongoing monitoring and board or executive assurance.

controls.title: Test systems as an attacker would
controls.statement: Conduct authorised penetration and adversarial testing at defined intervals and before significant deployment or change, using qualified testers and controlled rules of engagement.
controls.risk: Exploitable weaknesses may remain hidden until a real attacker uses them if testing never combines vulnerabilities into realistic attack paths.
controls.scope: External and internal systems, applications, APIs, hosted services, network paths, physical premises where applicable, testers and rules of engagement.
controls.examine: Review the testing program, risk-based scope, frequency, pre-deployment and change triggers, tester qualifications, independence, authorisation, safety limits and reports.
controls.interview: Ask service owners and testers how critical attack paths are selected, operational harm is prevented and exclusions or constraints affect assurance.
controls.test: Trace a sample of critical and recently changed services to completed testing and verify that authorised scenarios covered realistic internal, external and application attack paths.
controls.expected: Critical and changed services receive timely, authorised testing by qualified people, with controlled execution and clear, reproducible findings.

mappings.basis: Requires vulnerability assessment and penetration testing before deployment, before significant changes and at least every six months.

Requires a penetration-testing program with defined scope, frequency, limitations, contacts, remediation routing and retrospectives.
Requires at least annual external penetration testing by a qualified party.
Requires periodic and trigger-based security testing, including penetration testing, for internally developed or tailored applications.

Describes progression from manual pre-deployment testing to integrated static, dynamic and expert analysis.

controls.title: Remediate and verify assurance findings
controls.statement: Assign, prioritise and track assessment findings to an accepted resolution, then verify that remediation works and update detection or control design where needed.
controls.risk: Repeated assessments provide little protection if serious findings remain open, ineffective fixes are accepted or the same attack succeeds again.
controls.scope: Findings from control assessments, penetration tests, audits and continuous monitoring, including remediation plans, owners, due dates, exceptions and retests.
controls.examine: Reconcile assessment reports with remediation plans, risk ratings, owners, deadlines, accepted exceptions, closure evidence, retest results and resulting control changes.
controls.interview: Ask finding owners and risk owners how priorities are agreed, overdue work is escalated and closure is independently verified.
controls.test: Sample high, overdue and closed findings and confirm ownership and treatment decisions, then repeat the relevant check to verify that closed weaknesses are no longer exploitable.
controls.expected: Findings remain visible until an authorised resolution, overdue actions are escalated, and closure is supported by a successful retest or equivalent verification.

mappings.basis: Requires the system owner to produce a plan of action and milestones after a security control assessment.
Requires assessment reports to include recommended remediation actions alongside control-effectiveness findings.
Requires a maintained plan of action and milestones for weaknesses found through assessments, audits and monitoring.
Requires penetration-test findings to be remediated according to defined scope and priority.
Requires security measures to be validated after testing and detection capabilities to be updated where needed.
